The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) was established in October 1863 [1]. The ICRC resonated well with patriotic sentiments that were on the rise in the late-nineteenth century, and national societies were often encouraged as signifiers of national moral superiority [2]. The ICRC adopted its official name, the International Committee of the Red Cross, in 1876 [2]. Five years later, the American Red Cross was founded through the efforts of Clara Barton [2].

The ophthalmic nerve (first division of fifth cranial nerve, ophthalmic division of trigeminal nerve, CN V1, latin: nervus ophthalmicus) is the first branch of the trigeminal nerve [1]. This nerve carries sensory information from the scalp and forehead, the upper eyelid, the conjunctiva and cornea of the eye, the nose (including the tip of the nose, except alae nasi), the nasal mucosa, the frontal sinuses, and parts of the meninges (the dura and blood vessels) [2]. The ophthalmic nerve exits the skull through the superior orbital fissure [2].

The human musculoskeletal system (also known as the locomotor system) is an organ system that includes the bones, muscles, cartilage, tendons, ligaments, joints, and other connective tissue that supports and binds tissues and organs together [1]. It serves to provide form, support, stability, and movement to the body [1]. The musculoskeletal system includes the skeletal portion that serves as the main storage and provides the shape and form for the body, support and protection, allows bodily movement, and produces blood [2]. The muscular system is another part of the musculoskeletal system, consisting of skeletal, smooth, and cardiac muscles, which permits movement of the body, maintains posture, and circulates blood throughout the body [3]. Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) are injuries or pain in the human musculoskeletal system, including the joints, ligaments, muscles, nerves, tendons, and structures that support limbs, neck, and back [4].

The United States abandoned the gold standard in April 1933 [4]. This came after a series of moves led by President Roosevelt in March and April 1933, which caused the dollar's value to sink [1]. The Pax Romana is a term that refers to a period of relative peace and stability experienced by the Roman Empire between 27 BC and AD 180, inaugurated by the accession of Caesar Augustus and marked by the Roman principate [3]. This organization was created in 1921 by student leaders from 23 countries who met in Fribourg, Switzerland to create an international union for peace in response to World War I [4]. The organization has a special consultative status with the Economic, Social and Cultural Council (ECOSOC) of the United Nations [5].

The Ottoman Empire took Constantinople in 1453 [1], following the Battle of Kosovo in 1389 [1]. This marked a significant milestone in the Ottoman conquest, as the Empire then advanced into Greece, capturing Athens in 1458 [1]. The Greeks held out in the Peloponnese until 1460, and Venetian and Genoese clung to some of the islands until the early 16th century, but by this time most of mainland Greece and the Aegean islands were under Ottoman control [3]. The Despotate of the Morea, the last remnant of the Byzantine Empire, fell to the Ottomans in 1460, completing the conquest of mainland Greece [3]. Some parts of Greece remained under Ottoman control until the 20th century, but several coastal possessions were under Venetian control [4].

The longest human lifespan on record, according to various international bodies including the Gerontology Research Group and Guinness World Records, is 122 years and 164 days and is held by Jeanne Calment of France [1][2]. Susannah Mushatt Jones, who died in 2016, was the oldest living person at the time of her death [3].

The Clock Tower in Crouch End was built as a memorial to Henry Reader Williams in 1895 [2]. The Great Clock of Westminster, known as the Elizabeth Tower, was built by Edward John Dent on designs by Edmund Beckett Denison and entered service in 1859 [1]. The Clock Tower in St Albans, referred to as the "Clokkehouse" in 1412, has an astronomical clock built approximately 20 years after the death of Richard of Wallingford, the 29th abbot of St Albans [4].

The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, which ended the Mexican–American War, was signed on February 2, 1848, in Villa de Guadalupe Hidalgo (now a neighborhood of Mexico City) [1]. The treaty came into force on July 4, 1848 [1]. The treaty ceded what is now the states of California, Nevada, Utah, Colorado, Arizona, and New Mexico to the United States in exchange for $15,000,000 [4]. The treaty was ratified by the U.S. Senate on March 10, 1848, and by Mexico on May 19, 1848 [5].

The botanical name of lady finger is Caladenia catenata [1][2]. It is a plant in the orchid family Orchidaceae and is endemic to New South Wales, Queensland, and Victoria [1][2]. It is a ground orchid with a single hairy leaf and one or two white, sometimes pink flowers on a thin, sparsely-hairy stem [1][2].

The United Kingdom last won the Eurovision Song Contest in 1997 with "Love Shine a Light" by Katrina & the Waves [2]. The contest was held in Dublin, Ireland, and the United Kingdom went on to win with an unprecedented 227 points [2]. The 1997 contest is the most recent win for the United Kingdom [2]. Since the 1997 contest, the United Kingdom has not won or hosted the contest [3].

The downfall of the Inca Empire was primarily due to the Spanish conquest, which began in the 16th century [1][2][3]. This led to the political authority of the Inca state being ended, with the last ruler, Túpac Amaru, being captured and executed [1]. The Spanish also exploited the Inca mita corvée labor system for colonial aims and destroyed many aspects of Inca culture, including their farming system [1].

The collapse of the Inca population was largely due to infectious diseases carried by the Spanish colonists and conquistadors [2]. More people died of disease than in any army or armed conflict [2]. The population decline ratio in parts of the empire was 58:1 during the years 1520–1571 [2].

After the fall of the Inca Empire, efforts were made by the Spanish to quell Amerindian resistance and reorganize the country for gold and silver mining [3]. The last Inca resistance was suppressed in 1572 [3]. The indigenous population also suffered from exploitation, socioeconomic change, and epidemic diseases introduced by the Spanish [3].

Iker Casillas holds the record for the most clean sheets in La Liga with 1,275 minutes, a record that was previously the European record in a single season [1]. Petr Čech, on the other hand, holds a record for the fewest appearances required to reach 100 clean sheets in the Premier League, having achieved this in 180 league appearances [2]. In the Champions League, Casillas holds the record for most appearances, making his 152nd in a 2–1 home win over Chelsea [4]. Casillas also broke Edwin van der Sar's record for most clean sheets in Champions League history [4].

Tornadoes are more common in the United States than in any other country, occurring more than 1,200 times annually [1]. Most tornadoes in the United States occur east of the Rocky Mountains, with the Great Plains, the Midwest, the Mississippi Valley, and the southern United States being vulnerable areas [1]. While tornadoes have been reported in every U.S. state, including Alaska and Hawaii [2], the most tornado-prone places in the nation are the plains states [3]. The state with the most tornadoes per unit area is Florida, although most are weak tornadoes of EF0 or EF1 intensity [3][4]. Oklahoma has the highest number of strong tornadoes per unit area [3]. Tornadoes are less common west of the Rockies [1].
